title: What If You SWAPPED Bodies With Your Bully?
description:
Glint, 19, works nights at the city science museum. One night his old school bully, Dex Harlow, turns up as the cover night guard, mocks the new Swap Seats exhibit and slams his fist on the controls. A spark, a bang, and Glint wakes up six foot four, in Dex's body, while Dex is stuck in his. They have seven days to swap back before their brains redraw their body maps for good. Living Dex's life, Glint finds a tiny flat full of sticky notes, a dad who can barely stand, and an eight-year-old sister with a big operation coming. Living Glint's life, Dex finds out what it feels like to be called Goggles. The real science of the brain's body map (the homunculus, proprioception, the rubber hand illusion and the body-swap illusion) is the only way back.

If you swapped bodies with someone for one week, who would you choose? Tell me in the comments 👇

CHAPTERS
0:00 Cold open: Two hours
0:31 The Swap Seats exhibit
1:27 The Rules: your brain's body map
2:53 Minus: Everything is the wrong size
3:14 Plus: Strength
3:36 Minus: Always starving
3:49 Real head transplants
4:16 Plus: The flat
5:17 Minus: The Glint treatment
5:50 Minus: It's starting to fit
6:14 The Crisis: The swap locks at 2 a.m.
6:58 The Solution: See it, feel it, same moment
8:38 The Twist: The fact book
9:19 Would you?

SOURCES
• Penfield & Boldrey, Brain 60 (1937); Penfield & Rasmussen, The Cerebral Cortex of Man (1950): the body map in the brain and the homunculus
• Proske & Gandevia, Physiological Reviews 92 (2012): proprioception and the sense of limb position
• Botvinick & Cohen, Nature 391: 756 (1998): "Rubber hands 'feel' touch that eyes see"
• Petkovic & Ehrsson, PLoS ONE 3(12): e3832 (2008): "If I Were You: Perceptual Illusion of Body Swapping"
• Johansson & Westling, Experimental Brain Research 56 (1984); Gordon et al., Experimental Brain Research 83 (1991): grip force is set in advance from what the brain expects
• Resting energy use rises with fat-free (muscle) mass: e.g. Cunningham, American Journal of Clinical Nutrition 54 (1991)
• White et al., Surgery 70 (1971; operation 1970): head transplant in monkeys; the spinal cord could not be reconnected
• Canavero's announced human head transplant (2013 plan, 2017 announcements) never took place; no human head transplant has ever been performed
• Story is fiction: the swap, the seven-day lock and the swap back are made up; the science rules are real.
